To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a novel, highly efficient, environmentally friendly, and enantioselectively catalyzed Friedel-Craft reaction for the synthesis of various modified chromane derivatives with potential biological activity.
the rosin-derived tertiary-amine-thiourea-cocatalyzed Friedel-Craft reaction is highly enantio-selective and provides a new method for the synthesis of modified chromans with anticancer potency.
the rosin-derived tertiary amino-thiourea-cocatalyst is highly efficient for Friedel-Craft alkylation reaction of indoles with α,β-unsaturated aldehydes to give modified chromanes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and preliminary evaluation of the anticancer potency of modified chromanes.
the design and synthesis of novel modified chromanes via the highly enantio-selective Friedel-Craffts alkylation reaction, and their preliminary anticancer evaluation.

the design, synthesis, and preliminary biological evaluation (cytotoxicity) of a series of modified chromanes via the rosin-derived tertiary-amine-thiourea-cata-lyzed highly enantioslective Friedel-Craffs alkylation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synthesized chromanes are promising anticancer agents with a potential to be further optimized.
the synthesized compounds 4, 5, 6 and 7 showed good to very good cytotoxic activities with IC50 values ranging from 0.5 to 2.0 μg/mL.
this rosin-derived tertiary amino-thiourea-coupled Friedel-Craft reaction is a very promising method for the preparation of modified chromanes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a new method for the synthesis of chromanes via Friedel-Craft catalyzed alkylation of indoles.

we have developed a highly efficient catalytic system for the Friedel-Craft alkylation of aromatic ketones with 1-phenyl-3-(2,2-dimethyl-1,3-dioxolan-4-yl)propan-2-one to produce modified chromanes with high enantioselectivity and good yields.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a rosin-derived chiral tertiary amine-thiourae catalyst can catalyze a Friedel-Craft reaction with high enantioselectivity and that the resulting modified chromanes can exhibit anticancer activity.
this catalytic system can be used to synthesize various modified chromanes in high yield and enantioselectivity.

this new class of tertiary amine-thiouraeas can be used as a highly efficient and environmentally benign catalyst for the Friedel-Craft alkylation reaction of indoles with a wide variety of aldehydes, affording products in high yields with excellent diastereo- and enantioselectivities (up to >99% ee).
